title: Options Trading Mechanics: Market Makers, Margin Requirements, OCC Clearing, and Corporate Equity Derivatives
prerequisites: Call and put option definitions, strike price (K), stock price (S), and option premium (C or P)
Moneyness classifications: In-the-Money (ITM), At-the-Money (ATM), and Out-of-the-Money (OTM)
Standard 100-share North American stock option contract specifications
learningOutcomes: Explain the role of option exchange market makers, two-sided bid-offer quotes, percentage spread economics, and quote-splitting on multi-leg spread trades ([fact-01]).

Calculate initial margin requirements for naked (uncovered) call and put writers using the dual-formula maximum rules across ITM, ATM, OTM, and deep OTM scenarios ([fact-02], [fact-03], [fact-04], [fact-05]).
Describe daily mark-to-market collateral recomputation, margin calls, and excess collateral release for uncovered option writers ([fact-06]).

Trace the Options Clearing Corporation (OCC) clearing guarantee, exercise notice assignment methods (random, FIFO, equitable), automatic expiration exercise, and same-side position and 5-day exercise limits ([fact-07], [fact-08]).

Differentiate exchange-traded options from corporate-issued warrants, Employee Stock Options (ESOs), and convertible bonds with respect to issuer identity, maturity, transferability, and share dilution ([fact-09], [fact-10]).

misconceptions.misconception: Believing high leverage creates free profits without downside risk.
misconceptions.authorRebuttal: While a naked call's minimum margin floor uses 10% of the underlying stock value (C + 0.10*S) ([fact-02]), a naked put's minimum margin floor uses 10% of the total strike price value (P + 0.10*K) ([fact-04]). In the $50 ATM put example with P = $400 and K = $5,000, the minimum floor check is $400 + 0.10($5,000) = $900, which is compared against the primary formula result of $1,400 ([fact-05]).

misconceptions.misconception: Believing high leverage creates free profits without downside risk.
misconceptions.authorRebuttal: Exchange-traded options are issued by the OCC and settled strictly by transferring existing shares between secondary-market traders, so no new corporate shares are created and zero dilution of equity or EPS occurs ([fact-07], [fact-10]). Dilution only occurs when corporate-issued instruments—warrants, Employee Stock Options (ESOs), or convertible bonds—are exercised or converted, forcing the corporation to issue brand-new common shares ([fact-09], [fact-10]).

misconceptions.misconception: Believing high leverage creates free profits without downside risk.
misconceptions.authorRebuttal: Naked option positions are marked to market every single day using daily closing prices ([fact-06]). If the underlying stock moves adversely against the writer, required collateral increases and triggers a margin call; if the stock moves favorably, excess collateral is released back to the writer's margin account ([fact-06]).

activeRecallQuiz.scenario: A trader writes 1 naked XYZ July 50 call contract (100 shares, strike K = $5,000) when XYZ stock trades at $46 per share (S = $4,600) and the call premium is $2.00 per share (C = $200). The next day, XYZ stock surges to $55 per share (S = $5,500) and the call price rises to $7.00 (C = $700). Meanwhile, the company also has corporate warrants outstanding that are exercised by warrant holders.
activeRecallQuiz.question: 1) What is the trader's initial margin requirement at $46, how much additional collateral is required after the daily mark-to-market move to $55, and how much of the initial premium C can be applied toward collateral? 2) Does either the XYZ exchange-traded call or the corporate warrant exercise dilute the company's EPS?
activeRecallQuiz.correctAnswer: Correctly identifying the downside risk and margin constraints.
activeRecallQuiz.explanation: Detailed pedagogical explanation grounded in source principles.

coreTakeaways: Option exchange market makers provide continuous two-sided liquidity (Bid and Offer) strictly for their own accounts, earning the bid-offer spread (Offer - Bid) to compensate for inventory risk ([fact-01]).

Uncovered option writers must post initial margin equal to max(C + 0.20*S - OTM, C + 0.10*S) for calls and max(P + 0.20*S - OTM, P + 0.10*K) for puts—applying the upfront premium toward collateral—and are subject to daily mark-to-market recomputation ([fact-02], [fact-03], [fact-04], [fact-05], [fact-06]).

The OCC guarantees all exchange-listed options, manages random/FIFO exercise assignments, auto-exercises ITM options at expiration, and enforces same-side position/exercise limits ([fact-07], [fact-08]), whereas corporate-issued warrants, ESOs, and convertibles create new shares upon exercise and dilute existing shareholders ([fact-09], [fact-10]).
